documents.title: SIT Institutional Memory Platform — Detailed Design

questions.question: Are the objectives, the ten principles (P1-P10), the FR/NFR set and the confirmed decisions (Section 25) stated clearly enough to review against? Is the rule that the principle wins in a conflict usable when principles conflict with each other, for example P1/FR-16 agent backup against P2/P6/P7?
questions.rationale: Every later finding has to trace to a stated objective, requirement or decision, so ambiguous or conflicting intent must be found first.

queries: pgvector HNSW filtering WHERE clause post-filter ef_search
pgvector iterative index scans filtered search recall
pgvector partial index partition per tenant filtering
questions.question: Can pgvector HNSW with a separate B-tree index on (learner_id, slot_path) really restrict the search to 500-800 vectors per query? Or does HNSW filter after the index scan, so that filtered queries can return incomplete results and miss the NFR-2 latency/recall target?
questions.rationale: NFR-2 and the Section 12 sizing argument rest on this claim, and it decides whether the approved store choice meets its latency and recall objective.

queries: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server pgvector HNSW supported version
pgvector HNSW index size 1536 dimensions memory per million vectors
Azure PostgreSQL flexible server memory optimized 16 vCore 128 GB
questions.question: Does Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server in the Singapore region support pgvector with HNSW at the needed version? Do 128 GB RAM hold a ~57 GB raw vector set plus an ~80 GB HNSW index in memory, as the 'in-RAM index' latency claim assumes?
questions.rationale: The confirmed SKU decision and NFR-1/NFR-2 depend on the index fitting in memory at 9.5M vectors.

queries: PostgreSQL BM25 full text search ts_rank
Azure Database for PostgreSQL BM25 extension
questions.question: Is the BM25 keyword fallback in the Embedder realistic on Azure PostgreSQL, given that native full-text ranking (ts_rank) is not BM25? And is the read path specified for records flagged embedded:false?
questions.rationale: The Embedder fallback is the availability path for FR-10 reads when the embedding service fails.

questions.question: Are the following missing: a write-path error and feedback path (Validator or Classifier rejection after the agent has already received an ACK), dead-letter handling, idempotency or deduplication of retried Kafka messages, and read-your-writes or cache invalidation when a write lands during a cached session?
questions.rationale: FR-9/FR-10 make writes async and reads cached, so without these paths writes can be lost silently, duplicated or invisible, against P6/P7.

questions.question: Does the design define backup/restore, RPO/RTO, high availability for PostgreSQL, Redis and Event Hubs, the audit-store technology and its append-only enforcement, and retention or deletion propagation to Redis, the agent backup memory and the audit logs? Gaps the Pending Backlog already lists (Auditor retention, compaction, SIS failure handling) should be treated as acknowledged.
questions.rationale: NFR-7 retention enforcement and FR-15 deletion cannot be met if copies outside the primary tables are not covered.

questions.question: Do the numbers and statements agree across sections? Specifically: the per-learner breakdown (which sums to about 340) against the ~600 average; the MMP being outside the critical path (NFR-4) against Check 4 'MMP provisions slot' and PolicyEngine listed as an MMP component; orientation onboarding_progress typed WORKING (non-persistent) yet stored in a persisted slot; PUBLIC routed to memory_standard while the tier table lists INTERNAL+RESTRICTED only; and FR-9's order classify→embed→validate.
questions.rationale: The sizing, the availability claim (NFR-4) and the build-ready DDL and templates depend on these statements agreeing.

questions.question: Does P6 ('all writes are classified and policy-checked') conflict with the immediate agent-own-memory writeback in Section 14 phase 5? Does the cached-context-pack read path conflict with Section 16 'policy decisions are not cached', so that a policy change or revocation does not affect packs already cached?
questions.rationale: These are contradictions between principles and flows that P3/P6 and FR-8 rely on.

queries: Microsoft Entra ID access token lifetime default configurable
Entra ID configurable token lifetime policy retirement refresh token
Entra ID continuous access evaluation token revocation
questions.question: Can Microsoft Entra ID OAuth 2.0 issue or honour 48-hour access tokens? What are the default and configurable access/refresh token lifetimes, and how is revocation detected for a self-contained JWT?
questions.rationale: NFR-6, Gateway Check 3 and the confirmed 48-hour token decision depend on the identity provider actually supporting this behaviour.

queries: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server pricing memory optimized E16ds v5 Southeast Asia
Azure Event Hubs Kafka support tier standard pricing
questions.question: Is the SGD 800-1,200/month estimate credible for a Memory Optimised 16-vCore Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server in Southeast Asia, with storage, HA and backup? Is Event Hubs (Kafka-enabled tier), Redis and embedding cost included or excluded?
questions.rationale: NFR-10 is a stated cost constraint, and an underestimate would change governance and budget decisions.

queries: Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-small region availability Southeast Asia
Azure OpenAI data residency global standard deployment data zone
Singapore PDPA transfer limitation obligation overseas cloud
questions.question: Is Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-small available in an Azure Singapore (Southeast Asia) region or deployment type that keeps data in the region? Does sending HIGHLY_RESTRICTED counselling content to it raise data-residency or transfer concerns under the Singapore PDPA Transfer Limitation Obligation?
questions.rationale: The Embedder runs on all semantic writes, including the sensitive tier, so model availability and data location affect both feasibility and PDPA compliance.

queries: Singapore PDPA retention limitation obligation section 25
PDPA withdrawal of consent cease retain personal data
PDPC advisory guidelines key concepts protection obligation
questions.question: Does the per-agent per-learner backup (FR-16, 'survives learner self-deletion', 'full store always present for all learners') conflict with the FR-15 deletion promise, the P2/P4 counselling hard wall and the Singapore PDPA obligations on retention limitation, consent withdrawal and protection? Is the backup covered by the Gateway, the tiering and audit?
questions.rationale: A duplicate copy of learner and counselling data outside the governed path may undermine the platform's main privacy objectives.

questions.question: Is HIGHLY_RESTRICTED isolation preserved end to end? This covers Redis cache tiering, audit-log content (slot_path/key for counselling), Event Hubs topic-level access control, embedding deployment separation, the authentication model of the MMP Admin API (acknowledged as unspecified), Super Admin 'Everything' against the no-override promise, and serving backup data to a learner whose token is EXPIRED.
questions.rationale: FR-5/NFR-5 and P4 require the hard wall at every layer, not only in the PostgreSQL schema.

queries: Microsoft Entra ID UPN change immutable identifier oid recommendation
Entra ID oid claim vs upn use as user key
questions.question: Is using the mutable UPN as learner_id, the primary key everywhere, while the immutable oid is held as a secondary field, a risk to identity integrity and correct access control when a UPN changes or is reassigned?
questions.rationale: The confirmed learner_id decision affects how every namespace, audit entry and permission is linked to a learner.

queries: Azure Event Hubs Kafka dead letter retry consumer
Azure Event Hubs quotas limits partitions throughput units message size
Event Hubs at-least-once delivery checkpoint duplicates
questions.question: How do Azure Event Hubs in Kafka mode behave on consumer failure and retry? Is there automatic retry or a dead-letter queue, what is the delivery guarantee (at-least-once), and what limits apply to partitions, throughput units or message size? Does the claim 'failed writes queue and retry automatically' hold for the term-start spike?
questions.rationale: FR-9, NFR-3 and the Section 18 resilience claims depend on these broker semantics.

queries: pgvector HNSW build time memory maintenance_work_mem millions vectors
pgvector HNSW delete vacuum performance
questions.question: Does the design handle concurrent writes from several agents to the same slot, ordering per learner, audit volume (logging every cache hit across 15,000 learners), HNSW index build and maintenance at 9.5M vectors with deletions, and the 30-40M growth ceiling?
questions.rationale: NFR-1/NFR-2 and FR-13 must hold at the stated load and over time, not only for a static dataset.

questions.question: Which confirmed decisions rest on pending items? This includes Write path 'Kafka (Azure Event Hubs)' confirmed while Kafka vs Event Hubs is still in the backlog, the Redis choice, Auditor retention and PDPA sign-off, and the Dispatcher conflict resolution that FR-16/P1 depend on. What priority should each have before build?
questions.rationale: Decisions marked confirmed that depend on open items create rework risk for build phases 4-6.

questions.question: Can each acceptance criterion in Section 27 actually demonstrate its requirement? Examples: FR-5 tests only three agents and not the credential-level wall; FR-13 'exactly one entry per operation' under at-least-once delivery; the NFR-1 test without concurrent load; NFR-2's undefined 'normal load' and missing recall measure; FR-9 against NFR-3 tolerance; NFR-10 using measured data before build; FR-16 'does not attempt to write conflicting data'.
questions.rationale: Section 27 is the basis of the Phase 9 test plan, so criteria that cannot validate their requirement leave requirements unproven.

queries: filtered approximate nearest neighbor search benchmark recall
ANN benchmark recall latency methodology
questions.question: Is there a recognised benchmark method for filtered approximate-nearest-neighbour latency together with recall (for example ann-benchmarks style recall@k at a target QPS) that should be added to the NFR-2 benchmark?
questions.rationale: Measuring latency without recall can pass NFR-2 while filtered HNSW returns empty or incomplete results.

questions.question: Can the likely refinements (pgvector filtering strategy such as partitioning or iterative scans, governed agent backup, token lifetime handling via refresh tokens, write-error feedback) be made while preserving the confirmed decisions on pgvector, the 48-hour window, async Kafka writes and automatic write-back? Which, if any, would need an explicit challenge backed by at least two pieces of evidence?
questions.rationale: Refinements must respect approved decisions unless strong evidence shows a decision cannot meet an objective.

questions.question: Are accountable owners named for template approval, sensitivity and retention policy (DPO), Super Admin emergency access, the PDPA sign-off, pending backlog items and cost monitoring? Are operational monitoring and alerting defined for the data plane (consumer lag, embedding backlog, cache hit rate, audit-store health), and not only for the MMP dashboard?
questions.rationale: The governance and PDPA objectives need accountable decisions and operational visibility, and the document lists roles but not owners or closure dates.
